highlights.title: Coevolved Agent Training: virtuous cycle of co-improving planner and scorer, runaway divergence risks, and collusion failure modes
highlights.general_claim: A coevolved training loop pairing a planner agent and a scorer agent via DPO on synthetic preference data can produce a virtuous cycle of mutual capability improvement, but risks runaway divergence and inter-agent collusion.

highlights.title: Domain-Specific Engineering versus General-Purpose Scaling
highlights.general_claim: Scaling general-purpose reinforcement learning models outperforms domain-specific hand-engineered systems on competitive programming benchmarks.

highlights.title: System-level patterns for production readiness: integration architecture, pattern chaining, and maturity mapping
highlights.general_claim: System-level architectural patterns for agentic AI (authentication, event-driven reactivity, registries, and compliance monitoring) should be adopted progressively according to a GenAI maturity model rather than all at once, to match system complexity and risk profile.

highlights.title: New AI Models May 2026: The Frontier Took a Breath, Architecture Took the Stage
highlights.general_claim: April 2026 saw major frontier AI model releases that broke previous performance ceilings, but May 2026 pivoted toward architectural innovations and inference efficiency as the primary competitive focus.

highlights.title: Constraint Decay: The Fragility of LLM Agents in Backend Code Generation
highlights.general_claim: LLM agents' performance on backend code generation degrades significantly as structural constraints accumulate, with framework-specific sensitivities and data-layer defects being key failure modes.

top_picks.title: The Price Reversal Phenomenon: When Cheaper Reasoning Models Cost More
top_picks.summary_text: This paper investigates whether listed API prices of reasoning models accurately reflect actual inference costs. Evaluating 8 frontier models on 12 diverse tasks, the authors found a "pricing reversal phenomenon" where 32% of cheaper-listed models cost substantially more in practice. Specific example: Gemini 3 Flash is 80% cheaper by listed price yet 38% more expensive in actual total cost. Using Shapley value attribution, they traced this to vast differences in token efficiency, with models varying by up to 900% in thinking token usage and 10x in interaction turns. Repeated runs of identical queries show 9.7x thinking token variation, establishing fundamental limits on per-query cost prediction. The paper calls for cost-aware model selection and per-request cost transparency rather than relying on nominal API prices.
top_picks.general_claim: Listed API prices for reasoning models are unreliable proxies for actual inference costs because models with lower unit prices can require substantially more total tokens due to differences in efficiency.

top_picks.title: Constraint Decay: The Fragility of LLM Agents in Backend Code Generation
top_picks.summary_text: This paper presents a systematic empirical study of LLM agent performance on backend code generation under varying degrees of structural constraints. The researchers evaluated agents on 80 greenfield and 20 feature-implementation tasks across 8 web frameworks using an OpenAPI-based evaluation framework with end-to-end behavioral tests and static verifiers. Key findings identify a "constraint decay" phenomenon where agent performance declines substantially as structural requirements accumulate, with capable configurations losing 30 points on average in assertion pass rates. Framework analysis reveals significant disparities: agents perform better on lightweight, explicit frameworks like Flask than on convention-heavy environments like FastAPI and Django. Error analysis identifies data-layer defects, including incorrect query composition and ORM runtime violations, as the primary failure mode. The work highlights that joint satisfaction of functional and structural requirements remains a significant open challenge for coding agents.
top_picks.general_claim: LLM agents' performance on backend code generation degrades significantly as structural constraints accumulate, with framework-specific sensitivities and data-layer defects being key failure modes.
